seams.title: Attributed capture
seams.producer: person, sensor, controller, source system, or model
seams.invariant: Every accepted event preserves source identity, event time, receipt time, payload identity, freshness, authority scope, lineage, and transport state.
seams.degradation_law: A missing or damaged source is recorded as missing or damaged; the system may not synthesize an unattributed replacement.

seams.title: Identity resolution without collapse
seams.producer: attributed events and existing entity records
seams.invariant: Aliases, uncertain matches, and conflicting identifiers remain explicit until evidence supports a merge; replacement hardware or heads do not create a new mission identity.
seams.degradation_law: When identity confidence falls, the registry branches or marks uncertainty instead of collapsing distinct objects.

seams.title: Deterministic state compilation
seams.consumer: current mission, people, equipment, and communications state
seams.invariant: The same accepted event prefix reconstructs the same state and exposes stale, uncertain, and contradictory branches.
seams.degradation_law: Loss of the model or network may reduce interpretation and freshness but may not make accepted state unreconstructable.

seams.title: Source-bound relevance selection
seams.consumer: role aperture, deterministic query, or model context
seams.invariant: Every selected fact retains its source references, and every declared omission or context bound remains visible.
seams.degradation_law: When context or bandwidth shrinks, the system returns a smaller attributed slice and an omission record rather than an unbounded summary.

seams.title: Role-scoped projection
seams.consumer: named human, team, device, or controller surface
seams.invariant: Different roles may receive different projections, but no role surface silently changes the underlying state or leaks forbidden fields.
seams.degradation_law: A degraded role surface may lose convenience or detail while preserving source references, handling rules, and the ability to request escalation.

seams.title: Bounded stochastic interpretation
seams.producer: model or analytic runtime over a source-bound input
seams.consumer: candidate explanation, classification, warning, or option
seams.invariant: Interpretation remains a candidate with exact model, runtime, hardware, input, uncertainty, and evidence identities; it never becomes source truth or action authority by itself.
seams.degradation_law: When the preferred model is absent, the system falls back to smaller tools, deterministic query, queued work, or explicit abstention.

seams.title: Named authority disposition
seams.producer: candidate judgment and current authority state
seams.consumer: hold, refusal, safe state, approved request, or human-required queue
seams.invariant: A named human, controller, policy, mandate, operator witness, or lease supplies disposition authority; the model cannot accept itself.
seams.degradation_law: Missing, stale, or conflicting authority narrows the permitted action set and may force hold, refusal, or safe state.

seams.title: Idempotent bounded execution
seams.consumer: controller, workflow, message route, or other effecting system
seams.invariant: Each effect binds a bounded request, current state, idempotency key, timeout, safety rule, and rollback or compensation boundary.
seams.degradation_law: When execution authority or the effecting system is unavailable, the request remains queued, refused, or safely compensated without duplicate side effects.

seams.title: Outcome and acceptance receipt
seams.producer: effecting system, human reviewer, or external grader
seams.invariant: Process exit, model narration, or intended effect never substitutes for the observed outcome and responsible acceptance or rejection.
seams.degradation_law: If the outcome cannot be observed or independently accepted, the result remains partial, error, or held.

seams.title: Source-preserving synchronization
seams.consumer: peer node, reachback, or enterprise consumer
seams.invariant: Synchronization transfers attributed deltas and acknowledgments without turning the most connected or prestigious source into automatic truth.
seams.degradation_law: When links disappear, deltas queue locally with age and route state; when links return, both source histories remain inspectable.

seams.title: Explicit survival degradation
seams.consumer: local capability projection and human surface
seams.invariant: Lost streams, routes, compute, or convenience are named explicitly while identity, accepted state, evidence, authority, and basic human access remain available.
seams.degradation_law: Burst cognition and remote services shed before the deterministic survival substrate.

seams.title: Branch-preserving reconciliation
seams.consumer: named human or explicit superseding authority
seams.invariant: Reconnection preserves both branches, exposes conflicts and staleness, and records the named reconciliation disposition.
seams.degradation_law: Without a valid human or superseding authority, the conflict remains unresolved and visible.

seams.title: Component and vendor substitution
seams.producer: replacement model, runtime, head, adapter, compute, RF, or storage provider
seams.consumer: same mission and capability contract under a new treatment identity
seams.invariant: A component may be upgraded, removed, or replaced while state, evidence, interfaces, rollback, and independent verification remain available.
seams.degradation_law: An unqualified replacement remains isolated or held; the prior accepted path and neutral fallback remain recoverable.

seams.title: Durable byte and lineage custody
seams.producer: source, state, model, runtime, effect, and outcome artifacts
seams.consumer: later verifier, maintainer, replacement head, or after-action review
seams.invariant: Exact bytes, identities, manifests, lineage, and acceptance records survive beyond the process, provider, and current machine.
seams.degradation_law: Caches and optional raw media may be shed before manifests, authority, event history, and accepted evidence.

seams.title: Human and task reattachment
seams.consumer: returning operator on the same or replacement surface
seams.invariant: The operator returns to the exact pending decision, changes, evidence, and authority context rather than reconstructing a transcript manually.
seams.degradation_law: A reduced surface may present a smaller packet, but it retains the decision identity, receipts, and next valid actions.

seams.title: Visible resource placement
seams.consumer: CPU, RAM, NVMe, network, GPU, and remote worker assignments
seams.invariant: Every placement names the actual resource, memory boundary, link, power state, and fallback; separate GPUs never masquerade as pooled memory.
seams.degradation_law: When the preferred resource disappears or cannot fit the work, the scheduler serializes, reroutes, degrades, or refuses visibly.

seams.title: Cooperative track handoff
seams.producer: one sensor, controller, or node losing observation custody
seams.consumer: next sensor, controller, or node assuming observation custody
seams.invariant: Target or object continuity preserves identity, timing, uncertainty, coverage gap, and the exact handoff between observers.
seams.degradation_law: When cooperative coverage breaks, the track becomes stale, uncertain, or lost explicitly instead of being silently extrapolated as current.

seams.title: Human shift and role handoff
seams.producer: outgoing human, current state, and unresolved decision queue
seams.invariant: The handoff preserves what changed, what remains unresolved, who owns each decision, which evidence supports it, and which acknowledgments are missing.
seams.degradation_law: A short handoff may compress detail but may not omit pending authority, consequential conflict, or the path to the supporting evidence.

negative_witnesses.title: Unattributed input becomes state
negative_witnesses.mechanism: A report or sensor value enters the state without a source, time, digest, or transport identity.
negative_witnesses.refusal_condition: Reject or quarantine the event until the required attribution envelope exists.

negative_witnesses.title: Uncertain identities collapse silently
negative_witnesses.mechanism: Two people, devices, tracks, parts, or assets are merged because their labels look similar.
negative_witnesses.refusal_condition: Preserve separate identities or an explicit uncertain-alias relation until merge evidence exists.

negative_witnesses.title: Same history yields different state
negative_witnesses.mechanism: Runtime order, model output, or hidden mutable state changes the compiled result for the same accepted event prefix.
negative_witnesses.refusal_condition: Reject the reducer or state artifact when deterministic replay fails.

negative_witnesses.title: Context selection hides its sources and omissions
negative_witnesses.mechanism: A role surface or model receives a summary without the selected source identities or declared omissions.
negative_witnesses.refusal_condition: Hold the product until selection and omission receipts are available.

negative_witnesses.title: Role projection leaks or rewrites state
negative_witnesses.mechanism: A role-specific view exposes forbidden fields or changes shared state to fit the view.
negative_witnesses.refusal_condition: Reject the projection while preserving the underlying state and handling rules.

negative_witnesses.title: Model recommendation becomes authority
negative_witnesses.mechanism: A model-generated candidate is treated as accepted truth or executable disposition without a separate authority check.
negative_witnesses.refusal_condition: Require a named authority disposition and preserve the model output as a candidate only.

negative_witnesses.title: Stale mandate authorizes action
negative_witnesses.mechanism: An expired lease, missing operator witness, or superseded policy remains treated as current authority.
negative_witnesses.refusal_condition: Narrow the permitted action set to hold, refusal, safe state, or human-required review.

negative_witnesses.title: Retry duplicates an external effect
negative_witnesses.mechanism: A process restart or delivery retry repeats a message, controller command, or workflow mutation.
negative_witnesses.refusal_condition: Require an idempotency key and prior-effect lookup before execution.

negative_witnesses.title: Narration or process exit becomes success
negative_witnesses.mechanism: The system accepts the model's claim, a green process exit, or an intended effect without observing the outcome.
negative_witnesses.refusal_condition: Hold or reject the result until an outcome and external acceptance receipt exist.

negative_witnesses.title: Better-connected source overwrites local history
negative_witnesses.mechanism: A headquarters, enterprise, vendor, or remote model claim silently replaces the local branch because of source prestige or connectivity.
negative_witnesses.refusal_condition: Preserve both attributed branches and route disagreement to reconciliation.

negative_witnesses.title: WAN or burst GPU becomes the survival path
negative_witnesses.mechanism: Loss of remote services or the large GPU removes local identity, accepted state, evidence, authority, or basic human access.
negative_witnesses.refusal_condition: Reject the topology because optional layers must shed before the survival substrate.

negative_witnesses.title: Reconciliation hides a divergent branch
negative_witnesses.mechanism: Returned connectivity resolves disagreement automatically or discards one history without named disposition.
negative_witnesses.refusal_condition: Keep the conflict visible until a named human or explicit superseding authority resolves it.

negative_witnesses.title: Removing a provider destroys the capability
negative_witnesses.mechanism: State, boot, update, RF, model deployment, evidence, or recovery depends on one irreplaceable vendor path.
negative_witnesses.refusal_condition: Hold the sovereignty claim until rip-out, fallback, rollback, and independent verification pass.

negative_witnesses.title: Archive survives without verifiable custody
negative_witnesses.mechanism: Files remain present but their exact bytes, lineage, manifest, or acceptance identity cannot be verified later.
negative_witnesses.refusal_condition: Reject the archive or product until detached verification succeeds.

negative_witnesses.title: Returning operator must reconstruct the thread
negative_witnesses.mechanism: The system preserves logs but loses the pending decision, changes, evidence, authority, and next valid actions.
negative_witnesses.refusal_condition: Hold the handoff until an exact reattachment packet can be reconstructed.

negative_witnesses.title: Resource topology is concealed or fictional
negative_witnesses.mechanism: Separate GPUs are described as pooled memory, or CPU spill, link limits, thermal throttling, and worker loss are hidden behind one endpoint label.
negative_witnesses.refusal_condition: Reject the placement claim until exact resource and topology receipts exist.

negative_witnesses.title: Track handoff invents continuity
negative_witnesses.mechanism: A target or object is treated as continuously observed across a sensor or node transition without a bounded identity and timing handoff.
negative_witnesses.refusal_condition: Mark the track uncertain, stale, or lost until the handoff is evidenced.

negative_witnesses.title: Shift handoff loses the decision context
negative_witnesses.mechanism: The incoming person receives a narrative summary without unresolved decisions, authority, missing acknowledgments, or evidence paths.
negative_witnesses.refusal_condition: Require an attributed handoff packet and incoming acknowledgment.
